# 0.4 Parity, divisibility, GCD via Euclid, basic modular arithmetic

Phase 0 (Foundations), target rating 800–1000. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Parity arguments (`parity`)

Decide possibility or the answer from whether a sum, count, or difference is even or odd.

**Works because:** Every allowed operation keeps (or flips in a known way) the parity of some quantity, so parity is an invariant.

### Divisibility and remainders (`divisibility`)

Questions about multiples, remainders, ceilings of quotients, or counting multiples of k in [l, r] as r/k − (l−1)/k.

**Works because:** The condition depends only on values modulo k, or on whether k divides a quantity.

### GCD and LCM via Euclid (`gcd-lcm`)

Compute or reason about the greatest common divisor of two numbers or an array, and the least common multiple as a / gcd(a, b) · b.

**Works because:** gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), and gcd(a, b) = gcd(a, b − a), so subtractions and remainders keep the GCD.

### Arithmetic modulo m (`mod-arithmetic-basic`)

Compute a large sum or product modulo m by reducing after every step (no division).

**Works because:** (a + b) mod m and (a · b) mod m depend only on a mod m and b mod m.
